scenario: [LNUL.4.9] the null subject answers TRUE on null, which is the control for LNUL.4.9a. Same eval arm, subject IS_SUBJECT_NULL, un-negated, over a slot holding null. The rule fires, so `is null` is not merely `not (is <tag>)` — the two subjects are read independently off the value's tag. Paired with LNUL.4.9a deliberately: 4.9a proves the operator answers on absence at all, this proves it answers the RIGHT way for the one subject absence satisfies. fact_count 2.
rules_ds:
schema Sensor scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    state: Float? mutable

schema Marker scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

rule r:
    Sensor s where s.state is null
->
    emit Marker logical entity_id: s.entity_id
